text:
The Turin-based start-up CarpeCarbon and Michelin Italiana have signed an agreement to develop a project for the capture and utilisation of atmospheric CO₂ at the multinational’s tyre factory in Cuneo. This involves the construction of CarpeCarbon’s first industrial plant, which utilises its proprietary direct air capture (DAC) technology and integrates it into a production process, following the completion in December 2025 of the pilot plant at its headquarters in Caselle, near Turin.

The project with Michelin

Under the agreement, the project will make CO₂ captured directly from the atmosphere available for specific industrial applications at the site, helping to replace a portion of the carbon dioxide that Michelin receives from external suppliers. In addition, the portion of captured CO₂ that is not supplied to Michelin will be managed independently by CarpeCarbon and will be used for storage and the generation of carbon credits (in this case, certified as CO₂ equivalent removals).

The plant, representing an investment of two million euros, will have a nominal capacity of 300 tonnes of CO₂ per year. It is scheduled to come into operation in the second half of 2027.

The outlook

CarpeCarbon aims to increase its total carbon capture capacity to 5,000 tonnes per year by 2028–2029 and to 50,000 tonnes by 2030, through a growth model based on modular systems that can be integrated directly into existing industrial sites, powered at low temperatures (for example, by waste heat available on site), and on stand-alone modular systems powered exclusively by solar heat, again with low energy requirements.

The plant

“We have developed a proprietary technology, covered by three patents, and invested in the construction of a pilot plant. Being able to start implementing this plan alongside a leading industrial player such as Michelin Italiana is important for accelerating the subsequent phases of the technology’s industrial development. We are working to ensure that this serves as the starting point for extending the model to many other manufacturing companies in Italia, Europe and around the world,” emphasises Giuliano Antoniciello, co-founder and CEO of CarpeCarbon.

text:
Global computing developer NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) has acquired a strategic minority equity stake in Cambridge-based quantum error correction (QEC) startup Riverlane. Announced alongside corporate investments in four UK artificial intelligence ventures, the deal strengthens NVIDIA’s alignment with Riverlane’s physical QEC decoder stack (Deltaflow QEC) and expands its broader $250 million UK computing commitment.

Coinciding with the strategic investment, Riverlane and NVIDIA revealed an expanded technical collaboration demonstrating the use of NVIDIA H100 GPUs to accelerate real-time QEC decoder recalibration workflows. By adapting Riverlane’s Local Clustering Decoder (LCD) for high-throughput GPU parallel processing, a surface code training cycle that previously took 3 minutes on a single CPU core was reduced to 2.8 seconds. The H100 GPU processed over 4 million surface code error syndromes per second (compared to ~59,000 on CPU), enabling routine, pre-experiment decoder recalibration to mitigate dynamic qubit drift and hardware defects.

Mitigating Dynamic Qubit Drift via High-Throughput GPU Calibration

A primary bottleneck in scaling fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) is hardware instability: qubit frequencies shift, two-qubit gate fidelities fluctuate, and physical defects appear over time. Standard QEC decoders rely on pre-computed error likelihood weights; as physical qubit behavior drifts, these weights become inaccurate, degrading logical qubit fidelities.

By leveraging NVIDIA GPUs to process large batches of experimental syndrome data in parallel, Riverlane’s AI-driven calibration loop dynamically updates the decoder’s physical noise model in real time without manual tuning. The integration creates a tightly coupled QPU-GPU control loop where classical GPU acceleration continuously recalibrates low-latency hardware decoders (such as Riverlane’s ASIC/FPGA matrix chips), establishing a foundation for reliable, multi-modal utility-scale quantum systems.

text:
GOOCHLAND, Va. (WWBT) - Pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly broke ground Thursday on a $5 billion manufacturing facility in Goochland County’s West Creek area, marking a major step forward for one of Central Virginia’s largest economic development projects.

The facility, located along West Creek Parkway, is expected to bring approximately 1,800 construction jobs to the region, followed by 650 permanent positions once manufacturing operations begin.

The company announced the $5 billion project in September 2025, during former Gov. Glenn Youngkin’s administration.

Gov. Abigail Spanberger, who attended Thursday’s ceremony, acknowledged the work of her predecessor’s administration in bringing the project to Virginia.

Spanberger also revealed that the company’s original plans called for a significantly smaller investment.

“The original plans that Lilly put forward called for a $2.1 billion investment. And they have more than doubled it,” Spanberger said.

Part of a nationwide manufacturing expansion

The Goochland project is part of Eli Lilly’s broader $50 billion commitment to expand pharmaceutical manufacturing in the United States.

Ricks said the Richmond-area facility is one of 10 new U.S. manufacturing sites announced by the company and one of five focused on producing active pharmaceutical ingredients — the components responsible for a medicine’s therapeutic effects.

The company has experienced rapid growth, fueled in part by demand for its diabetes and weight-loss medications, Mounjaro and Zepbound.

However, those medications will not be the focus of the Goochland facility.

Instead, the company plans to manufacture advanced biologic medicines, including therapies being developed to treat cancer and potentially autoimmune diseases.

A first-of-its-kind facility for Lilly

According to company leaders, the Goochland site will be Lilly’s first fully integrated manufacturing facility dedicated to its emerging bioconjugate platform and monoclonal antibody portfolio.

The facility will handle the process from producing active pharmaceutical ingredients to manufacturing finished medicines at a single location.

Ricks said that approach will give the company greater control over production while reducing its reliance on foreign suppliers.

“What makes this site unique is that it will bring API production together with finished medicine,” Ricks said. “So it will literally run the whole process here at Richmond.”

Among the treatments planned for the facility are antibody-drug conjugates, or ADCs, which combine an antibody designed to target cancer cells with a powerful cancer-fighting drug.

The goal is to deliver treatment more precisely to tumors while limiting damage to surrounding healthy tissue and potentially reducing side effects.

The facility is also expected to incorporate artificial intelligence, machine learning and advanced analytics into its manufacturing operations. Lilly is targeting LEED Gold certification, an environmental building standard.

Alongside the manufacturing project, Lilly announced a $40 million commitment to the Virginia Center for Advanced Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, a workforce development initiative involving industry, government and higher education partners.

The initiative will include a hands-on pharmaceutical manufacturing training center in Goochland County, targeted to open in 2028.

The training is intended to help Virginians develop skills for careers in pharmaceutical manufacturing, including people who have never worked in the industry.

The facility’s permanent positions are expected to include engineers, scientists, manufacturing operators and laboratory technicians.

“In Virginia, we have made workforce development a top priority because the jobs being created by this project, they will need to be filled, and they need to be filled by Virginians,” Spanberger said.

Lilly officials said work to prepare the site and recruit employees has already begun.

While the project promises significant economic investment, company leaders acknowledged that construction could cause temporary disruptions for people living and traveling near West Creek.

Ricks said the scale of the project could affect traffic patterns and create other disturbances as construction progresses.

“Let me begin by apologizing for any disturbance,” Ricks said. “Progress takes some of that from time to time.”

He thanked neighbors for their patience and said Lilly wants to hear community feedback as work continues.

The company expects construction of the facility to be completed by 2030.

Additional commissioning and regulatory approvals will be necessary before full manufacturing operations can begin.

The Richmond facility is planned as Lilly's first U.S. site to house both active ingredient production and finished-dose manufacturing on one campus.

Lilly has signed a major collaboration with METiS TechBio to apply AI to new lipid nanoparticle drug delivery platforms for tissue-targeted therapies.

The Richmond buildout and METiS TechBio partnership only capture part of how Eli Lilly is repositioning its long-term oncology and delivery capabilities. Our analysis turns up 1 warning sign for Eli Lilly as well.

This push into AI-enabled drug delivery and advanced manufacturing extends far beyond Eli Lilly. Investors may want to explore broader healthcare AI exposure through 37 healthcare AI stocks.

Eli Lilly is a large US pharmaceuticals group that develops and sells human medicines across major global markets. This Richmond build and the METiS TechBio alliance speak directly to how its oncology and drug delivery pipeline is being set up inside a broad commercial footprint.

3 things going right for Eli Lilly that this headline doesn't cover.

How does the Richmond ADC facility reshape Eli Lilly's business model?

The Richmond site links active ingredient production and finished-dose manufacturing for antibody drug conjugates on one campus, which tightens control over a complex supply chain. That integrated setup can reduce coordination risk across contractors and gives Eli Lilly more flexibility to match future oncology and autoimmune demand with in house capacity.

Does this Richmond and METiS news change the Eli Lilly Narrative?

It leans into the existing Narrative rather than rewriting it. Analysts already frame incretin drugs as the earnings engine, with big U.S. manufacturing projects and non incretin portfolios in oncology and immunology as supporting catalysts. Richmond ADC production and the AI driven METiS LNP work both sit squarely in that capacity and pipeline expansion story.

See how these catalysts shape Eli Lilly's path to a $1,329 fair value.

What could go wrong in execution for Eli Lilly here?

Richmond requires large up front capital and a highly skilled workforce, so construction delays, hiring gaps or regulatory setbacks could push out when that ADC capacity becomes usable. On the METiS side, technical hurdles in tissue specific lipid nanoparticles or safety issues in early programs would limit how quickly those delivery platforms can feed into commercial candidates.

What is the key sign over the next 2 to 3 years that will show if this thesis is working?

The clearest checkpoint is whether Richmond hits its targeted operational timeline around 2028 with ADC output ramping as planned, alongside at least one METiS partnered LNP program advancing into later stage trials. If capital spend climbs without those concrete milestones, the case for this build out as a long term earnings support weakens.

Eli Lilly's factories, alliances and trial pipelines get headlines, but the quieter story is who approves those moves, how their incentives are wired, and what that means for your capital over time. See who is actually steering Eli Lilly, and how they are paid.

text:
Microsoft says its medical AI system can diagnose difficult cases more than twice as accurately as practicing doctors.

Dubbed the Microsoft AI Diagnostic Orchestrator (MAI-DxO), the system “substantially outperformed practicing generalist physicians” in diagnostic accuracy while ordering fewer tests and procedures, according to a newly published paper.

The Microsoft study, titled “Sequential Diagnosis with Language Models,” was first posted online last year on arXiv as a non-peer-reviewed preprint. On Thursday, the findings were finally published in the peer-reviewed journal Science.

That’s a major step toward validating the findings, but any real-world deployment would still require clinical testing, Microsoft’s AI chief Mustafa Suleyman told The Verge. Microsoft already has plans for that: the company’s AI health lead, Dr. Dominic King, told the publication that testing will begin at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, Massachusetts, within the next couple of months.

In tests involving complex medical cases published in The New England Journal of Medicine, DxO achieved 83.2% diagnostic accuracy, compared with 36.1% for generalist physicians who had access to reference materials. When physicians were denied those resources, their accuracy dropped to roughly 22%, making DxO nearly four times as accurate. In a separate test involving emergency department admissions, Microsoft’s AI again outperformed generalist physicians, though by a narrower margin of 80.3% to 46.8%. The system achieved its strongest results using OpenAI’s GPT-5, with additional testing showing improvements using GPT-5.5.

“It also manages to do this at half or even one third of the cost, getting to the right diagnosis with fewer tests and procedures,” Microsoft said in a blog post Thursday. Those savings, however, are based on estimated costs in simulated cases rather than actual medical expenses. The researchers admitted that they “would expect the performance gap to narrow” if DxO were compared with expert specialists rather than generalists.

Notably, DxO works sequentially, meaning patients don’t simply present the system with a comprehensive list of symptoms, medical history, and test results. Instead, it starts with a chief complaint and must determine which follow-up questions to ask and tests to order before arriving at a diagnosis. That’s much closer to how doctors actually diagnose patients. The researchers say benchmarks have previously failed to evaluate LLMs’ diagnostic capabilities sequentially and propose a new benchmark called the Sequential Diagnosis Benchmark, or SDBench.

DxO “simulates a panel of physicians,” the paper explains, “continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests.” The system assigns different roles to AI agents that propose diagnoses, select tests, challenge assumptions, and weigh costs. Researchers suggest this approach can help counter some of the cognitive biases that affect individual physicians, such as anchoring on an initial diagnosis or overlooking alternative explanations.

Similar claims have been made about other companies’ AI tools. Earlier this year, researchers from Harvard University and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center found that OpenAI’s o1-preview reasoning model outperformed physicians in diagnosing emergency room patients during triage.

Is KDP a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on KDP. This isn't the first time we see a beverage company pitched as a great investment. KDP shares gained 25.12% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Coca-Cola Consolidated (COKE) and The Coca-Cola Company (KO) gained 64.19% and 32.51%, respectively, during the same period. Familiar brands and repeat purchases can attract investors, but rising share prices also raise expectations. Does KDP still offer an attractive buying opportunity after its rally, or have investors already priced in much of the upside?

Pixabay/Public Domain

In June, we published an article about the 10 Undervalued Counter Cyclical Stocks to Buy Now and KDP ranked #1 in that article. KDP gained 7.71% since then. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on KDP. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. (NASDAQ:KDP) owns and distributes a broad range of non-alcoholic beverages while also running one of the largest single-serve coffee systems through Keurig brewers and K-Cup pods. Its brands include Dr Pepper, Canada Dry, Snapple, Ghost, Electrolit, and Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, and the April 2026 acquisition of JDE Peet's greatly expanded its global coffee business. The central investment debate is whether that acquisition and the planned split of the company can boost earnings and create enough value to make up for the large debt taken on to pay for the deal.

Over the past twelve months, revenue reached $20.1 billion, up 27.5% from a year earlier, though much of that growth came from adding JDE Peet's rather than from the existing business growing on its own. Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. trades at about 31.7 times its past earnings, well above the peer median of 18.4 times, but that drops to roughly 13.7 times when looking at expected future earnings. This gap suggests investors are not paying only for today's business, they are betting that the acquisition and separation will produce a much stronger earnings base.

The optimistic view rests mainly on the $18.4 billion JDE Peet's deal and the idea that the combined company can create more value once it splits into two independent businesses. Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. completed the purchase in April 2026, adding coffee brands such as Jacobs, L'OR, and Peet's, while steady demand for Dr Pepper, Ghost energy drinks, and Electrolit hydration products continues to support the beverage side. Management plans to separate the company into a standalone refreshment beverage business and a standalone global coffee business by early 2027, giving investors two distinct companies instead of one.

Management expects 2026 net sales of $25.9 billion to $26.4 billion, which shows how much larger the business is set to become with the coffee operations and U.S. refreshment beverages combined. If Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. can bring JDE Peet's smoothly into the fold, capture cost savings, and keep up momentum in energy, hydration, functional, and zero-sugar drinks, bulls believe each business will have a clearer strategy and a more focused approach to spending its cash. If that happens, earnings should recover meaningfully from today's depressed level, which is why the earnings multiple looks far cheaper on future profits than on past ones. The company also generated $1.5 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2025, which gives management some room to pay down debt before the split.

Analysts are also supportive. Their average 12-month price target of $36.21 implies about 15% upside from the $31.39 share price, while the median target is $38 and individual estimates range from $29 to $42. Those targets rest on expected earnings per share of $2.29, which is more than double the $0.99 the company earned over the past twelve months. Put simply, the targets assume Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. will be valued at a fairly ordinary level once profits rebound. Because the gap between past and expected earnings is so large, investors should watch closely whether the benefits of the deal and operating improvements actually show up, as a slower recovery would make these targets harder to justify.

The latest quarter shows why integration and debt are the key risks. The JDE Peet's deal is adding a lot of revenue, so you would expect profits to hold up as the business grows, but they have not. Gross margin, which shows how much of each sales dollar is left after the direct cost of making products, fell sharply from a year earlier, and both operating income and earnings per share dropped noticeably. At the same time, interest costs have climbed almost twofold, since Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. carries about $28.5 billion of net debt after the deal. Shrinking margins, rising interest costs, and heavy debt just before a major split raise real questions about how well management can execute. You can check out whether Keurig Dr Pepper's $925 million exit from Chobani is a smart reset here.

Another risk for the stock is weakening demand within Keurig's single-serve coffee system. Its recurring pod sales depend on households continuing to use its brewers and buy compatible coffee. In 2025, U.S. K-Cup pod volumes fell 4.8%, while brewer volumes dropped 19.9%, reflecting price sensitivity and other pressures. Weaker brewer sales could slow household adoption, although replacement purchases and retailer inventory changes also affect those figures. If consumers buy fewer pods or switch brewing methods, coffee sales could struggle even with successful acquisition integration. Price increases may support revenue temporarily while masking lower consumption. In our opinion, this could limit KDP's price multiples if its expanded coffee business lacks sustained underlying demand growth.

Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 47 hedge fund portfolios held Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. at the end of the second quarter, up from 43 in the previous quarter. This modest rise suggests institutional investors are still fairly optimistic about the integration, the planned separation, and the earnings recovery, despite concerns over debt and margins. By comparison, The Coca-Cola Company (NYSE:KO) was held by 90 hedge funds, up from 76, while PepsiCo, Inc. (NASDAQ:PEP) was held by 68 hedge funds, down from 72, and Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc. (NASDAQ:COKE) was held by 33, up from 31. Overall, institutions grew most confident in The Coca-Cola Company, interest in Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. also improved, PepsiCo, Inc. lost some support, and Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc. saw only a small gain relatively.

Short interest data also paints a somewhat cautious picture for Keurig Dr Pepper Inc., with 6.03% of its shares available for trading sold short, well above The Coca-Cola Company at 1.24% and PepsiCo, Inc. at 1.90%. It is, however, slightly below Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc., where 6.79% of shares are sold short. This suggests the integration, debt, margin pressure, and planned split are drawing more scrutiny for Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. than for The Coca-Cola Company and PepsiCo, Inc., though negative sentiment is still a little milder than for Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc.

Valuation Analysis

KDP's EV/EBITDA is 16.74x. The Coca-Cola Company, Coca-Cola Consolidated, Inc., and PepsiCo, Inc. trade at EV/EBITDA multiples of 20.48x, 13.72x, and 12.12x, respectively. KDP's own EV/EBITDA was 15.41x on December 31, 2025, approximately 9% below its current multiple, although the JDE Peet's acquisition limits comparability because trailing EBITDA includes only part of the acquired business's earnings. We believe the current valuation reflects expectations that acquisition savings and the planned separation will improve profitability, balanced against concerns about debt and weakening coffee demand. However, its headline premium of approximately 22% to Coca-Cola Consolidated and 38% to PepsiCo means the discount to Coca-Cola alone does not establish that KDP is inexpensive. Management expects 4%–6% constant-currency adjusted EPS growth from the legacy business in 2026, but supporting the EBITDA valuation will also require acquisition savings to improve operating profits and translate into cash after interest and capital spending. We believe KDP can justify its current valuation if the combined business generates enough cash to reduce debt while sustaining underlying growth, rather than relying mainly on acquired revenue. If management restores margins and completes the separation without weakening either business, KDP could be a good long-term investment, although we would prefer a lower entry price given its leverage and integration risks.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on The Coca-Cola Company (KO) by Rijnberk InvestInsights in February 2025, which highlighted strong organic growth, pricing power, volume growth, margin expansion, and its defensive dividend profile. KO's stock price has appreciated by approximately 28.13% since our coverage. We believe KDP could be a good long-term investment at a lower price, as its current valuation leaves limited room for setbacks in margin recovery, debt reduction, and acquisition integration.

Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. Health insurance provider Elevance Health (NYSE: ELV) reported Q3 2026 results beating Wall Street’s revenue expectations, but sales were flat year on year at $50.44 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $6.99 per share was 48.9% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

StockStory’s take

Elevance Health’s third quarter results were defined by stronger-than-expected performance in government and individual health lines, particularly Medicaid, Medicare Advantage, and Individual ACA. Management pointed to focused execution and recent Medicaid rate actions as key contributors, with CEO Gail Boudreaux highlighting, “These results reflect focused execution across the enterprise.” Operational improvements in Carelon and disciplined cost management also supported the company’s outperformance relative to Wall Street expectations.

Looking forward, management raised its full-year adjusted earnings outlook, citing confidence in continued margin improvement across health benefits and the growing contribution of Carelon’s value-based solutions. CFO Mark Kaye emphasized, “We remain confident in delivering at least 12% adjusted EPS growth in 2027 from this higher baseline.” The company’s strategy centers on integrating medical and pharmacy offerings, expanding Carelon’s external reach, and advancing cost management through technology and clinical oversight.

Key insights from management’s remarks

Management attributed the quarter’s results to disciplined cost controls, improved Medicaid rate alignment, and expanded adoption of Carelon’s integrated solutions, which together drove better operating performance in several core business lines.

Medicaid margin stabilization: Recent rate increases and targeted clinical management actions helped stabilize Medicaid margins and set up the segment for improvement in 2027. Management noted ongoing efforts to align rates with cost trends and proactively address behavioral health utilization.

CarelonRx and value-based care: Strong operating performance in CarelonRx was driven by integration of medical and pharmacy benefits, with members in integrated plans experiencing fewer emergency room visits and significant per-member-per-month savings. The introduction of specialized programs, like the Oncology Center of Excellence, has enhanced patient outcomes and operational efficiency.

Commercial segment pricing discipline: The Commercial business benefited from prudent pricing and a focus on affordable, integrated solutions. Management underscored the importance of alternative funding models and highlighted wins in the large employer space, including clients returning to Anthem offerings after brief absences.

Medicare Advantage repositioning: Deliberate changes in product and market focus for Medicare Advantage led to improved quality mix and operating margins. Management is prioritizing HMO plans and dual-eligible members, aiming to further increase the share of members in higher-rated plans.

AI and analytics in cost management: The company is increasingly leveraging AI-enabled analytics to identify abnormal utilization patterns, particularly in behavioral health and payment integrity. These efforts have contributed to early identification of cost drivers and expedited corrective actions, with notable impact on claims management and fraud detection.

Drivers of future performance

Elevance Health’s full-year outlook is shaped by margin recovery in Medicaid, continued Carelon expansion, and operational efficiency initiatives.

Medicaid margin improvement: Management expects Medicaid margins to begin recovering in 2027 as state rates better reflect underlying cost trends and targeted interventions in behavioral health and care management take hold. However, the pace of recovery depends on how quickly states incorporate higher costs into rate-setting and the impact of new work requirements.

Carelon external growth and integration: The company is scaling Carelon’s offerings beyond affiliated health plans, focusing on external client wins in behavioral health, pharmacy, and post-acute care. Leadership highlighted high retention rates and a robust sales pipeline, supporting expectations for Carelon to become a larger contributor to enterprise earnings.

Commercial and ACA market discipline: In the Commercial segment, pricing for stability amid elevated cost trends is a priority, while ACA market performance benefits from product mix shifts and disciplined rate filings. Management cautions that the risk pool in ACA will take more than one cycle to normalize as enhanced subsidies expire.

Catalysts in upcoming quarters

In the coming quarters, the StockStory team will watch (1) the pace of Medicaid margin recovery as rate adjustments and care management initiatives progress, (2) Carelon’s success in expanding its external client base and executing on integrated value-based care, and (3) the commercial segment’s ability to maintain pricing discipline amid cost trend pressures. Developments in regulatory policy, particularly around work requirements and IDR, will also be key for future performance.

text:
Eli Lilly and Company broke ground Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, on a $5 billion manufacturing facility in Goochland County, Virginia, just west of Richmond, moving its first fully integrated plant for active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished medicines from plan to construction. The Indianapolis-based drugmaker said the site will focus on antibody-drug conjugates, a class of targeted cancer treatments, and is expected to employ about 650 people once running, with roughly 1,800 workers needed during construction.

How antibody-drug conjugates are made

Antibody-drug conjugates combine a monoclonal antibody, which seeks out a specific marker on a cell, with a potent drug payload attached through a chemical linker. The design aims to deliver a cell-killing agent directly to tumor cells while limiting exposure to healthy tissue. Lilly said in its announcement that these medicines are being developed for cancer and are also being explored for autoimmune diseases and other conditions.

Producing them is technically demanding because it joins two very different manufacturing worlds. The antibody comes from large-scale biologics production in living cells, while the payload and linker are small-molecule chemistry, often involving highly potent compounds that require containment. The conjugation step that links them, followed by purification and fill-finish, adds further handling and quality requirements. Many developers split these steps across several plants or outside contractors, which makes Lilly's decision to house API and drug product in one facility the central operational feature of the Virginia project.

When Lilly first announced the site in September 2025, it described the plant as its first dedicated, fully integrated site for its bioconjugate platform and monoclonal antibody portfolio and said it expected construction to be completed within five years.

Industry implications

The groundbreaking turns a commitment Lilly first disclosed in 2025 into physical construction. Lilly framed the project as one of 10 new U.S. manufacturing sites it has announced since 2020, including five that will produce API: Richmond; Huntsville, Ala.; Houston; and two sites in Lebanon, Ind. Its other new U.S. sites cover injectable medicines and devices in Research Triangle Park and Concord, N.C., Kenosha, Wis., and Lehigh Valley, Pa., plus a genetic medicines site in Lebanon.

For the broader drug industry, the Virginia plant signals that targeted oncology biologics are now being treated as volume products that justify dedicated domestic capacity, rather than niche therapies made in small batches. Lilly's emphasis on digital tools for "right-first-time execution" also reflects a shift toward data-driven quality control in complex biologics, where batch failures carry high costs.

The project also lands amid federal pressure to reshore drug production. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer spoke at the event and tied the investment to the resilience of the American economy, underscoring the policy weight now attached to domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Competitive and supply chain implications

Integrating API and finished product under one roof reduces the number of handoffs between facilities, a common source of delay and risk for complex biologics. For Lilly, that could mean tighter control over timelines and quality as its oncology pipeline advances. For contract development and manufacturing organizations that specialize in conjugation and high-potency handling, a large in-house plant from a major drugmaker may limit some future outsourcing opportunities, even as demand from smaller developers continues.

The build also creates near-term demand for suppliers of bioreactors, chromatography systems, containment equipment, automation software and cleanroom construction. Lilly has not disclosed equipment vendors or contractors for the site. Rivals that rely heavily on overseas or third-party capacity for antibody-drug conjugates may face pressure to explain their own domestic supply plans to regulators and payers.

Workforce availability is a practical constraint. Highly potent compound handling and biologics operations require specialized technicians, which helps explain Lilly's $40 million commitment to a statewide training network rather than relying solely on local hiring.

Regional implications

The facility strengthens the Richmond region's emerging biopharmaceutical manufacturing base. Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger called the investment a powerful vote of confidence in the state, and Goochland County Board of Supervisors Chairman Jonathan Christy described the groundbreaking as an exciting step forward for the community.

The training center planned for 2028 gives the region a pipeline for skilled operators that could also serve other drug manufacturers. In its 2025 announcement, Lilly said job creation support would come in part through the Virginia Talent Accelerator Program and that its investment and job figures exceeded what it first committed in its state incentive application. The roughly 1,800 construction jobs will add near-term activity for regional trades and contractors.

What comes next

Site construction in Goochland County, with Lilly hiring for permanent roles in the Richmond area as building progresses.

Opening of the Virginia Center for Advanced Pharmaceutical Manufacturing training center in Goochland County, targeted for 2028.

Equipment installation, commissioning and validation ahead of regulatory approval for commercial supply, within the five-year completion window Lilly outlined in 2025.

Further construction milestones at Lilly's other new U.S. API sites, including Huntsville and Houston.

Updates on the antibody-drug conjugate programs that the facility is designed to supply.

Sources

Eli Lilly and Company: Lilly announces plans to build $5 billion manufacturing facility in Virginia (Sept. 16, 2025)

text:
L'Oreal said Thursday its third quarter sales rose by double digits as the French cosmetics giant appeared to have dodged the stagnation affecting much of the luxury industry.

The company, whose brands include Garnier, Lancome and Maybelline, said its sales came in at 11.6 billion euros ($13.0 billion) in the three months to the end of September, handily beating analyst expectations.

That is an 11.9-percent increase from the same period last year, with growth in all divisions, including the luxury unit.

Chief executive Nicolas Hieronimus called L'Oreal's third quarter performance "exceptional".

"The global beauty market, once again, proved its resilience in a challenging context -- and we continued to significantly outpace it," he said.

He reaffirmed his confidence that L'Oreal will manage to increase its sales and profits again this year, but did not provide any figures.

Sales rose in all regions, including in the company's North Asia region.

It said China had been the key driver, its sales there advancing nearly three times faster than the overall market, with the luxury segment also growing.

China was the main driver of growth in the luxury market until recent years.

L'Oreal has largely been able to avoid the troubles that luxury groups have faced thanks to its products aimed at the mass market and professionals.

text:
Amélie Thiriet comes from LVMH’s hotel holding company, where she oversaw the sales, marketing, and communication functions. This entity brings together the luxury group’s own hotel activities, including Cheval Blanc and, since 2019, Belmond. Her profile is geared toward brand development and international sales in upscale hospitality. The new CEO succeeds Gilda Perez-Alvarado, who had led Orient Express since January 2024 alongside her role as head of strategy for the Accor group.

Since the opening of Orient Express La Minerva in Rome or the launch of La Dolce Vita Orient Express train in April 2025, the brand’s portfolio has been gradually moving from sales pitch to actual operations. On the agenda are the Orient Express Venezia hotel which opened in March 2026, the Orient Express Sailing Yachts with the Corinthian (named in April 2026) and the Olympian in preparation, and then the announced return of the historic Orient Express train in 2027.

In June 2024, Accor and LVMH sealed a strategic partnership around Orient Express. LVMH took a stake in the brand, in the company that operates the future hotels and trains, and in the entity that owns the two sailing yachts. The arrival of an executive coming directly from LVMH Hotel Management at the head of an Accor brand reflects the operational rollout of this agreement.

This story was originally published on Banking Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily Banking Dive newsletter.

Barclays is cutting roughly 5,000 full-time employees, or 5% of its workforce, this year – with heavy impact expected in "support functions" such as developers – as artificial intelligence boosts productivity, the bank's CFO, Anna Cross, said Thursday.

The announcement came as the British bank reported its third-quarter earnings, which revealed, among other metrics, a 19% year-over-year drop in revenue from fixed income and currency trading.

The job cuts stole the show, though. Barclays reduced its workforce by about 1,000 employees in the first half of the year, so the remaining 4,000 jobs are expected to be shed by December.

"The changes that we're making in the third and fourth quarters of this year are sizable," Cross told analysts on a call Thursday. "They relate both to the simplification of the organization and to some of the impacts that we're starting to see from AI."

Barclays CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan, colloquially known as Venkat, noted the bank intends to "employ AI at scale."

"But AI is the icing on the cake, not the cake," Venkat said.

Barclays is far from the only bank this year to hang workforce cuts on the rise of AI.

HSBC in March was reported to have been considering shedding as many as 20,000 mostly middle- and back-office jobs over the next five years in favor of AI.

Standard Chartered in May said it would eliminate more than 7,800 "corporate functions" jobs, such as human resources, risk management and regulatory compliance, by 2030.

But StanChart CEO Bill Winters' description of the jobs that would be replaced rankled some observers.

"It's not cost cutting; it's replacing, in some cases, lower-value human capital with the financial capital and the investment capital we're putting in," Winters said during the bank's May investor day. "We don't have job losses, but we do have job role reductions in favor of the machines, and that will accelerate as we go forward into AI."

Winters later apologized amid public criticism that he appeared to be assigning value to the workers inhabiting those roles.

"Where roles do fall away, it reflects changes in the work, not the value of our people," Winters said in a memo the next day.

Barclays' Venkat, as it turns out, offered a more tempered assessment of Winters' comments as the StanChart blowback grew.

"What people do are jobs, and a job is much more than a collection of tasks," Venkat told Bloomberg in May. "Now you've just got to take tasks and make them more productive."

Roughly 60% of the Barclays jobs on the chopping block are so-called support functions. The bank said it had spent £307 million ($410.5 million) over the first nine months of 2026 on a restructuring that has included staff reductions, investments in technology and a broader overhaul of operations. Barclays expects to incur another £300 million in restructuring costs by the end of December, the bank said.

The total, more than £600 million, is roughly double the bank's earlier estimate. Barclays, however, is sticking to its cost estimates for 2027 and 2028, Cross said.

On the earnings front, Venkat said he is "disappointed" by the dip in fixed income.

"This is always the house that fixed income built," he said. "You can be sure this will get my attention."

Not all of Barclays' earnings news should come as negative, though. The bank reported third-quarter profit of $3.1 billion, a 12% increase from a year ago.

Barclays' equities traders, meanwhile, posted a 47% jump in revenue.

text:
The only constant is change, as the saying goes, and workers are wearing thin because of it.

Organizational change isn’t new, but many companies have undergone great upheaval since the Covid-19 pandemic: navigating hybrid work and return-to-office mandates, mass layoffs, restructurings and the consequent reshuffling of responsibilities, and AI adoption.

“Everybody is feeling change fatigue,” Lorraine “Lo” Stomski, Walmart’s chief talent officer, told CNBC Make It at Forbes’ Future of Work Summit in New York City on Oct. 6. “The environment is changing so rapidly.”

Managers and employers should be thinking about “really helping their employees to navigate through that,” she adds.

Change fatigue is a state of exhaustion workers may experience after going through many changes at their employer. It can show up as resistance, apathy, or resignation to changes, and research indicates it can predict increased strain and burnout, as well as lower employee commitment and performance.

Many employees are hit with curveball after curveball with little time to adjust. Roughly 73% of employees said their organization had experienced some level of disruptive change within the past year in a Gallup survey of over 22,000 U.S. workers published in December 2024. “The more disruption that employees have experienced, the more likely they are to feel burned out today,” the report says.

“Change is stressful, particularly if it’s not managed well,” says Peter Cappelli, management professor and director of the Center for Human Resources at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School. “Every transition creates stress and requires energy from people, and they just get worn out from doing it.”

Employers can take some steps to make changes feel more manageable, including “giving workers agency” and “equipping them with tools,” said Stomski.

That could mean getting their input on a restructuring ahead of time. Letting them apply for other jobs internally if their current role will be eliminated also helps, Cappelli adds: “You should certainly tell people what you’re trying to do, and then say we want to involve you in the process.”

Communicating clearly through the change, including specifying why it’s happening and how it will affect employees, can mitigate anxiety around it. When it comes to introducing new technologies, like AI, training can help things go over more smoothly.

“A lot of resistance comes from people who feel they’re going to fail in the new context,” Cappelli says. If you can demonstrate what it looks like and practice what they should do with it, that can help smooth the transition.

As for employees, while they likely won’t have much sway in the matter, they should focus on what they can control. They can also ask their direct managers for more answers and clarity that can ease the transition, Cappelli says. But organizations should expect some workers may also resort to looking for work elsewhere.

“Employees who are confronted with this kind of change, without a story about where it’s going, without any sense that they’re going to be involved in the process, without any control over it — I wouldn’t be surprised to find that they’re all going to be looking for another job,” Cappelli says.

Several groups have crowdfunded together to mount a legal action to try to stop Amazon Web Services' expansion in Aragon.

text:
ZARAGOZA, Spain — Aragon's rugged plains stretch out under a clear blue sky, the buildings visible as "a few tiny cubes sprawled like a throw of dice" across the terrain — as George Orwell wrote in Homage to Catalonia, of his time here during the Spanish Civil War in the 1930s. Today, excavators eat the earth, carving huge chunks of the landscape in the race to build the behemoths of the AI boom.

This drought-stricken region of northeast Spain has become the focus of American companies searching for locations to place their energy- and water-intensive data centers. In Aragon, Amazon Web Services promises to spend almost $40 billion to build multiple vast complexes — one alone as large as 600 American football fields. Microsoft and the asset management firm Blackstone are among those following suit, signing agreements to build data centers that will transform this region and the livelihoods of its inhabitants.

Even as other countries enact regulations to curb the expansion of data centers (and Spain's national government weighs new restrictions), Aragon's regional government is welcoming the companies with open arms. Touting themselves as the "Virginia of southern Europe" after the U.S. state with the largest concentration of data centers, they are taking the bet that hosting data centers will bring jobs and prepare the region for the economic shifts they believe AI will bring.

"This is a new economy that is evolving, and it's very difficult to foresee how many activities are going to be coming around it," said Eva Valle, the economic counsellor for the regional government. "But they are coming."

The companies were drawn to the region with promises of large tax breaks and fast-tracked planning permissions that give these data centers a special status usually reserved for the general interest of the local population. This order gives them the power to expropriate land, strips local mayors of veto powers, and restricts the time the public has to object to 23 working days. (For the recent Amazon Web Services development, the regional government opened the window to oppose the project over the Christmas period. Opponents of the project believe they did this to try to push it through at a time when people would be paying less attention, though the government denies this.)

The rapid approval process for these large and hyperscale facilities has left many in Aragon feeling excluded from decisions that will profoundly impact their region and lives.

"It's going to be like living beside a prison"

The first time Silvia Baselga and her family learned of the data center soon to tower over their home was when they noticed the survey markers poking out of the ground on the other side of their garden wall. "When we saw this, we went to the city hall and said, 'OK, we want information. This is really close to our house.'" But the local council told them they had no information. Only when the planning documents were later made public did they learn that the outer perimeter of the data center is to be built within 300 feet of their home in the hilltop village of Botorrita. The plans showed that the complex will be larger than the village itself.

Baselga's parents retired here for the tranquility of a life spent in a tight-knit village community. Their home looks out over fields and gently rolling hills. To try to block the noise the data center will emit, Baselga believes the company will build a 20-foot-high wall, as happened in a nearby village. "We're going to open the window and see nothing," she said. Friends regularly visit at night to gaze at the stars in this rural setting. Baselga said the center's 24-hour security lights will block out the night sky. "It's going to be like living beside a prison."

Centers like these are set to be built across Aragon — 27 in total, according to official documents — some by Spanish and other firms, but most by American companies, taking up about 7 square miles of land. At least one is built partly on ground originally classified as protected for natural ecosystems. The companies promise employment. Amazon Web Services told NPR it will create 6,200 permanent jobs once these centers are built. But many residents fear they will also deliver an environmental crisis.

Economic development "at the cost of the environment"

The data centers will consume many times the current electricity needs of the region and require large amounts of water to cool their servers in one of Spain's driest regions, one that's been repeatedly blighted by drought.

Julio Enfedaque drives across the parched land his family has farmed for generations. This year it barely rained for four months, and the government cut the amount of water available for irrigation by two-thirds. "Even if they say the data centers won't take the water that we need for agriculture, I am sure it's going to become very complicated to farm like my ancestors used to." Enfedaque has advised his nephews to find different careers and leave the land.

Amazon Web Services says its data centers will draw water only after temperatures hit 86 degrees Fahrenheit and that they are investing millions of dollars to help fix leaking water pipes and working with farmers to use AI technology to make their water use more efficient. "We're trying to not only use as less [sic] water as possible, but also to help those communities where we operate have the best infrastructure," David Blázquez, Amazon's head of public policy for Spain and Portugal, told NPR.

But the company remains opaque about how much water each center will use. Blázquez said it's "a company policy not to publish water usage per site." Regional figures show Amazon's three existing data centers, which are much smaller than what is planned, used 68 million liters — 48% more than the company had originally told regional officials they would need.

Endangering valuable habitat for rare and migratory birds

Perhaps an even bigger problem is the energy these centers need to run. Unlike many data centers in the U.S., which are powered by natural gas, companies in Aragon say they will rely mainly on renewable sources (though they also have diesel generators on site). Blázquez says Amazon Web Services has secured "a hundred renewable projects in Spain," including 17 in Aragon.

While that energy is carbon-free, ecologists and biologists warn that additional wind projects could have their own devastating consequences for the environment.

The region is full of hunting grounds for vultures and other birds of prey and an important stop for migrating birds.

"The vultures look for the thermal air currents to lift them. But they run straight into the windmills — for them it's like flying through knives," explained José Antonio Pinzolas, an ornithologist.

Aragon's own environmental agency has warned that wind farms in this area pose a high risk of collision to the endangered red kite and other protected raptors, and has documented an increase in bird and bat deaths in recent years as the renewable sector expands.

"I've collected ospreys, golden eagles, kestrels by the dozen, black vultures," said Juan Ballesteros, a nature protection officer for the local government.

Ballesteros used to love his job for its access to wildlife. Now, he said, he spends his days placing the corpses of birds killed by turbine blades into body bags. Ballesteros met NPR as he arrived to collect the body of a young Eurasian black vulture that lay dead on the ground, its wings splayed in the dirt at the foot of a wind turbine.

Blázquez told NPR, of the damage to this important habitat that the expansion of wind and solar farms causes, that Amazon Web Services "definitely shares those concerns." He said they work with renewable energy companies that comply with environmental legislation. But Pinzolas said the growing number of bird deaths shows the current protections in place are not working.

Environmental groups say the overall impact of wind turbines on birds isn't being properly assessed.

Several groups have crowdfunded together to mount a legal action to try to stop Amazon Web Services' expansion in Aragon. The court case challenges the Aragon government's fast-tracked approvals of the plans. "We have concerns about water consumption, about energy consumption, the impact on some other industries and on the environment," said Luis García,, an activist with Ecologistas En Accion, one of the organizations involved in the case. He said the economic benefits of data centers are not great enough to justify the "huge damage they do to the environment."

Locals fight to preserve nature for future generations

One recent weekend in the region's capital, Zaragoza, an avenue filled with demonstrators protesting against a new data center to be built at the edge of a forest by the city. Residents fear the heat and noise of the complex will destroy a tranquil space that is a haven during the hot summer months.

"This is a worthy fight as all the worlds invades us, to save this pine forests, to save the environment, against this voracious capitalism that thinks only of economic interests and not of people," said Marian Rams, a local resident with white hair dyed in hues of pink, green and blue. "They want to swap nature for data centers."

Nearby, a little girl no older than 5 chanted along with the demonstrators. Her mother, Ana Domezian, walked alongside her with her second child, a baby, nestled in a carrier against her chest. "If we don't fight now for what we have," she asked, "what are we going to leave to them in the future?"

text:
Most web pages run using an open-source programming language called PHP. That language is maintained by the PHP Foundation. Today, the foundation disclosed two “critical” software vulnerabilities and issued an emergency patch, urging websites to implement it immediately or take down their websites until they are able to. The vulnerabilities are named CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and collectively called “php2shell.”

As reports broke late on Oct. 20 of the vulnerabilities ahead of the patch’s official release, some opportunistic attackers tried to exploit it. Cloudflare, a global cybersecurity company that helps secure millions of websites, saw “tens of thousands” of exploit attempts within 45 minutes of the word getting out. That number jumped to “hundreds of thousands” within two hours, and millions by the evening of Oct. 21, according to seeing “early attacks,” according to its co-founder and CEO Matthew Prince.

Amazon Web Services also reported on Oct. 21 that the vulnerability is “now being broadly exploited in the wild.” The company said that it had seen some attempts by hackers to use the exploit in the days prior to the vulnerability being disclosed on Oct. 20, raising the possibility that the news about the flaw had leaked to hackers prior to the official announcement from PHP.

One startup owner reported that the PHP bug is “real bad” and says everyone should be “afraid” after hackers allegedly stole their source code, exposed cookie data, and leaked legal documents.

Multiple governments have decided to take websites offline as a safety precaution, including some agencies in the Netherlands and Finland, Reuters reported. The FBI’s cyber division and the National Security Agency both issued statements urging potentially affected organizations to update their services, as did the prime minister of Japan, the European Union’s computer emergency response team, and several other national agencies.

“The impact of the PHP vulnerabilities is massive, [and] can expose a large number of websites to immediate attacks if not patched in time,” Gang Wang, associate professor of computer science at the University of Illinois’s Grainger College of Engineering, told Fortune. The bugs allow bad actors to remotely execute code on flawed, not-yet-patched PHP systems. Attackers can use that as an “entry point into the network hosting that machine, and from there potentially carry out attacks that cause significant damage,” Wang’s colleague, David Nicol, director of the Information Trust Institute at Grainger College, told Fortune.

Among the most well known sites that run on PHP is WordPress, which powers roughly 40% of all websites, according to Reuters. But PHP is ubiquitous across the web, having started as a small project back in 1994 and grown up with the modern internet. For example, Facebook launched in 2004 as a PHP website, although in 2020 the company embarked on a major effort to update to different software. Other popular sites using PHP include Microsoft.com, Wikipedia.org, Archive.org (now temporarily offline), TheGuardian.com, and Baidu.com, according to W3Techs. An initial analysis by cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks identified 22.6 million potentially vulnerable instances.

OpenAI cofounder and president Greg Brockman said PHP was his “first programming language,” in a post about the vulnerability discovery. OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol model, as well as other AI tools, played a key role in finding the vulnerabilities.

“Given the severity of these flaws and PHP’s widespread use, we consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory,” OpenAI said in a blog post. “It highlights how AI can uncover security flaws with internet-scale impact, but the same capabilities can also help attackers rapidly develop offensive tools and exploits.”

The backstory: Three parties discovered different elements of the bug

Multiple security organizations independently found the issue around the same time, in August. All of them used AI to help find the vulnerabilities. They then banded together in a coordinated effort with the PHP Foundation to develop fixes and coordinate the disclosure of the vulnerabilities and rollout of the patch, OpenAI said.

Technically, the first to discover part of the issue was the California-based AI red-teaming firm Calif. OpenAI had invited Calif to join its Patch the Planet initiative, an effort to proactively find and patch security vulnerabilities in digital infrastructure. Calif decided to investigate PHP because it “stood out as a high-impact target,” the company says. It reached out to Volker Dusch at the PHP Foundation, and then “got to work hacking PHP.”

The Calif team was “not expecting to find anything critical” since PHP has been highly scrutinized by the cybersecurity community for years. In fact, the bug they eventually found had “been present in PHP for 14 years,” OpenAI’s Brockman pointed out in his post. “A limited version of it had been discovered in 2024 and wasn’t considered significant at the time.” But now that AI models can run attack sequences autonomously, almost no vulnerability is too difficult to exploit.

“Php2shell shows how AI can help uncover buried flaws and turn complex exploit chains into practical attacks, increasing the potential risk,” TJ Sayers, senior director of threat intelligence at the Center for Internet Security, told Fortune.

On Aug. 1, Calif found the first issue using GPT-5.6 Sol. It then informed OpenAI, which looked into the issue on its own and found additional elements of the bug. This made the discovery more comprehensive, but almost made clear that the flaw was more serious than Calif had originally realized, an OpenAI spokesperson told Fortune.

Then OpenAI began chatting with the PHP Foundation about the issue. Through those conversations, OpenAI learned that Wiz, a Google-owned cybersecurity company, was also talking to the foundation about the issue.

Researchers at Wiz had independently found the vulnerabilities in August. They decided to investigate PHP in the first place because it’s “the backbone of the internet,” a Wiz spokesperson tells Fortune, acknowledging that the parallel initiative may seem like a “coincidence,” but the Wiz team’s charter is to investigate high-impact digital infrastructure, and PHP was top of mind. The Wiz team identified the first issue on Aug. 19, using a combination of Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol, and Wiz Atlas.

“With 70% of the internet affected, the impact of php2shell cannot be overstated,” Wiz said in a blog post announcing its findings. “It marks an AI inflection point. The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade–what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.”

OpenAI then decided to bring all the parties together, leading a “coalition of maintainers, researchers, and security providers to address [the] critical vulnerabilities,” the company said. That included Wiz, Calif, PHP, Cloudflare, and multiple U.S. government agencies, among others. Cloudflare’s blog post also names the French cybersecurity company Quarkslab as part of the effort.

title: BKT ties up with Pirelli for premium car tyres as rivals commit ₹8600 crore to expansion

Apollo accounts for ₹5,810 crore, CEAT ₹1,314 crore, Bridgestone approximately ₹750 crore ($85 million) and Michelin nearly ₹686 crore.
BKT targets ₹23,000 crore in revenue by FY30, with on-highway tyres contributing approximately 20 per cent, or ₹4,600 crore.
BKT and Pirelli expect India’s premium car-tyre market to grow almost fivefold between 2025 and 2030, without disclosing its starting size.
For Pirelli, the partnership offers Indian manufacturing capacity; for BKT, the challenge is building a profitable passenger-car tyre business against established competitors.
text:
Balkrishna Industries (BKT) on Thursday announced a partnership with Italian tyre maker Pirelli to manufacture premium passenger car and SUV tyres at its Bhuj plant in Gujarat, targeting annual production of up to 8 lakh Pirelli-branded tyres by 2030. The companies have not disclosed when production will begin.

Rajiv Poddar, BKT’s Joint Managing Director, said the partnership would accelerate its existing plans to enter new tyre categories, describing Pirelli’s decision as “a recognition of the manufacturing strength, quality and expertise we have built over decades”.

Under three agreements signed on October 22, the companies plan a 50:50 joint venture to establish a new tyre factory in India, sharing manufacturing capacity equally. BKT will separately pay Pirelli in euros for testing and technical services covering its own passenger-car, SUV and two-wheeler tyres. The venture’s incorporation is targeted by December 31, 2030, although investment, capacity and commissioning details remain undisclosed.

The partnership comes as Bridgestone, Michelin, CEAT and Apollo Tyres have announced combined investments of approximately ₹8,600 crore to expand Indian production. Apollo accounts for ₹5,810 crore, CEAT ₹1,314 crore, Bridgestone approximately ₹750 crore ($85 million) and Michelin nearly ₹686 crore.

BKT has separately outlined a ₹6,800 crore investment programme through FY29 covering off-highway and on-highway tyres, carbon black and infrastructure. Whether the Pirelli venture requires additional investment remains unclear.

India’s premium tyre opportunity extends beyond luxury cars. SUVs account for more than half of passenger-vehicle sales, driving demand for larger 17-inch to 22-inch tyres. Electric vehicles require tyres designed for greater weight, higher torque and reduced noise, while the expanding vehicle population supports replacement demand.

Manufacturing orders, technology support

Under the initial offtake agreement, Pirelli has committed to minimum annual purchases, although year wise quantities, contract value and margins remain undisclosed. Pricing will reflect actual raw-material and conversion costs, providing demand visibility without guaranteeing profitability.

The arrangement gives BKT, traditionally an off-highway tyre specialist serving agriculture, mining and construction, an established premium customer while it develops its own passenger-car brand. Pirelli’s trademark and specified know-how can be used only for tyres supplied to Pirelli and its affiliates.

Marco Tronchetti Provera of Pirelli, said India’s economic development and growing demand for technologically advanced tyres made it important to the company’s international strategy.

BKT targets ₹23,000 crore in revenue by FY30, with on-highway tyres contributing approximately 20 per cent, or ₹4,600 crore.

Competition builds capacity

Bridgestone, which reported around 20 per cent of India’s passenger-vehicle replacement tyre market in 2024, plans to add 11 lakh tyres annually at Pune by 2029. CEAT plans another 35 lakh annually at Chennai by FY28, while Michelin is expanding premium-car tyre production and Apollo is adding passenger-car and commercial-vehicle capacity.

BKT and Pirelli expect India’s premium car-tyre market to grow almost fivefold between 2025 and 2030, without disclosing its starting size.

For Pirelli, the partnership offers Indian manufacturing capacity; for BKT, the challenge is building a profitable passenger-car tyre business against established competitors.

text:
Disciplined execution and tangible progress on the Group's strategic priorities in a challenging environment

Focused action plan to restore Gucci desirability and rebuild foundations for sustainable growth

Solid momentum at Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Brioni, Kering Jewelry and Kering Eyewear, with clear action plans to further unlock their full potential

Revenue : €3,345 million

Stable on a reported basis, -1% on a comparable basis

“Third-quarter revenue reflects the phasing we anticipated, in a softer macroeconomic environment.

The recovery of Gucci remains our defining priority. We are steadily strengthening desirability and advancing our product development at pace. Reflecting the complementarity of our portfolio, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta and Brioni, as well as Kering Eyewear and Kering Jewelry, continue to extend their strong trajectory and we are doubling down on the renewal of Balenciaga and Alexander McQueen.

Unlocking the Group's full potential requires restoring momentum at Gucci, accelerating on product excellence, delivering our action plan in China, realizing the full benefits of our Group platform and embedding a culture of execution across the organization.

The transformation of Kering is a multi-season undertaking, but the improvements we are seeing across the Group, notably in desirability and key operating indicators, reinforce our confidence in the direction we have set, and the determination of our teams to deliver it.”

Luca de Meo, Directeur général de Kering

Kering revenue in the third quarter of 2026 amounted to €3,345 million, stable as reported and down 1% on a comparable basis year-on-year. The change in reported revenue included a positive currency effect of 1 percentage point and no scope impact.

Third-quarter revenue reflected the anticipated second-half phasing and a more difficult comparison base, compounded by softer macroeconomic trends. Traffic remained the main constraint, while conversion, average price and average ticket remained supportive across most Houses, helped by stronger product execution and improved client engagement.

By channel, in the third quarter:

• Sales from the directly operated retail network, including e-commerce, declined by 3% on a comparable basis, remaining uneven across regions and Houses.

• Wholesale and Other revenues were up 3% on a comparable basis.

In the first nine months of 2026, the Group generated revenue of €10,565 million, down 2% as reported and stable on a comparable basis, while advancing the optimization of its store network. Following 75 net store closures in 2025, Kering completed a further 105 net store closures during the first nine months of the year, including 128 closures and 23 openings, thereby exceeding its full-year objective of 100 net closures ahead of schedule. The Group now plans at least 125 net closures for the full year 2026.

Kering Fashion & Leather Goods

In the third quarter of 2026, Kering Fashion & Leather Goods revenue amounted to €2,743 million, down 1% as reported and 3% on a comparable basis.

The performance of Gucci, which is part of this segment, is detailed in a dedicated section.

Sales in the directly operated retail network were down 4% on a comparable basis. Excluding Gucci, retail sales increased by 2%, driven by continued growth at Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta and Brioni, underscoring the increasing breadth of the Group’s portfolio.

• Saint Laurent growth was notably driven by sustained momentum in North America and Western Europe, and strong engagement from VICs (Very Important Clients) and Core clients.

• Bottega Veneta again outperformed across key markets, supported by sustained brand desirability, strong momentum in leather goods and successful product introductions. The House also advanced its diversification strategy, notably in ready-to-wear, while benefitting from strong engagement among VICs.

• Balenciaga remained resilient in leather goods, while its ready-to-wear and shoes categories were still challenged.

• Alexander McQueen pursued its repositioning, sharpening its British tailoring identity, enhancing its product offering and streamlining its distribution footprint as part of its turnaround plan.

• Brioni maintained strong growth, supported by its highly personalized client relationship and the strength of its bespoke offer.

Wholesale and Other revenues of the segment increased by 4% on a comparable basis.

of which Gucci

Gucci recorded revenue of €1,291 million in the third quarter, down 4% as reported and down 6% on a comparable basis.

The performance of Gucci reflected a more demanding comparison base and a less pronounced newness effect than in the second quarter. While traffic remained the main constraint, conversion, average price and average ticket improved further, supported by the progressive rollout of new collections.

The House pressed ahead with its product transformation agenda, further refining its product and pricing architecture, enhancing quality and improving time to market. Handbags were at the forefront of these efforts, supported by a richer offering, while ready-to-wear and shoes remain key areas of focus.

Sales from the directly operated retail network declined by 9% on a comparable basis. North America remained the House’s most resilient market against a more demanding comparison base, while lower traffic weighed on performance in Asia Pacific, particularly in Mainland China, and in Japan.

Wholesale and Other revenues were up 35% on a comparable basis in the third quarter. Wholesale, which amounted to €120 million, or 9% of the quarterly sales, was up 45% on a comparable basis, reflecting a low comparison base and order-book effects as new collections came through.

Kering Jewelry

In the third quarter of 2026, Kering Jewelry delivered another strong performance against a more demanding comparison base. Revenue amounted to €239 million, up 12% as reported and 11% on a comparable basis, reflecting the strength of the division’s complementary Houses.

Boucheron maintained strong momentum, supported by the enduring appeal of its iconic collections Quatre and Serpent Bohème and good performance in Japan and South Korea. Pomellato continued to build momentum, particularly in Japan, driven by sustained demand for Nudo, Iconica and Together. Performance at DoDo and Qeelin was mixed, though the Houses moved forward with their product initiatives, notably with Qeelin’s successful launch of Wulu Purple Jade.

Sales in the directly operated retail network increased by 18% on both a reported and a comparable basis, while Wholesale and Other revenues decreased by 6%.

Kering Eyewear

In the third quarter of 2026, Kering Eyewear revenue amounted to €373 million, up 6% as reported and up 4% on a comparable basis, reflecting the resilience of the business despite the anticipated phasing effects between the third and fourth quarters. Performance was supported by ongoing innovation and strong commercial execution across the portfolio, with growth across all regions. Key developments during the quarter included the launch of the Fall Winter 2026 collection of Maui Jim, initiatives celebrating the fortieth anniversary of Lindberg, as well as successful sales and marketing campaigns across key markets.

Corporate & Other

In the third quarter of 2026, revenue from Corporate & Other amounted to €27 million, down 5% on a reported and a comparable basis, primarily reflecting the end of rental income following the real estate transactions.

Within the segment, Ginori 1735 delivered strong double-digit growth, reflecting the steady progress in brand development and desirability across key markets.

Outlook

Kering is fully mobilized on the execution of its strategic plan. The Group continues to prioritize the quality of its revenue and the depth of its transformation, with progress on both fronts: several Houses are showing strong momentum and the recovery at Gucci is gradually taking shape.

While short-term revenue trends reflect a more challenging macroeconomic environment, Kering confirm its objective of improving its recurring operating margin in 2026, supported by the efficiency measures under way, while maintaining strong investment in the desirability of its Houses.

HIGHLIGHTS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS DURING THE THIRD QUARTER

Gucci and L’Oréal entered a 50-year exclusive beauty license, one year ahead of schedule

On July 7, 2026, Gucci and L’Oréal entered into a 50-year exclusive beauty license agreement, expected to become effective in mid-2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals and the early redemption of the existing agreement between Gucci and Coty. By combining the global desirability and distinctive creative vision of Gucci with the unparalleled expertise of L’Oréal in beauty, innovation capabilities and worldwide distribution network, the partnership aims to unlock significant long-term growth opportunities across fragrance and beauty.

Romain Spitzer appointed Chief Executive Officer of Bottega Veneta

On July 15, 2026, Romain Spitzer was appointed Chief Executive Officer of Bottega Veneta, effective since September 1, 2026. He reports to Luca de Meo and joins the Executive Committee of Kering. He brings more than thirty years of international experience in the luxury industry, with extensive expertise in brand

stewardship, retail excellence, and client experience.

Kering Jewelry leadership appointments

On September 1, 2026, Kering announced the appointment of Charlotte Fournet as Pomellato Chief Executive Officer and Krizia Cucurachi as DoDo Chief Executive Officer, both effective since September 15, 2026, and reporting to Jean-Marc Duplaix, Group Chief Operating Officer and Chief Executive Officer

of Kering Jewelry. These appointments support Kering Jewelry's ambition to further unlock the growth potential of its Houses while reinforcing their distinctive identities.

Sabina Belli appointed President of Kering Italia

On September 1, 2026, Sabina Belli was appointed President of Kering Italia, effective since September 15, 2026, reporting to Luca de Meo, Chief Executive Officer of Kering. In her new role, she represents Kering in Italy and strengthens the Group’s dialogue with public institutions, luxury industry associations and key stakeholders. In addition, she continues to oversee the Kering Accademia per le Eccellenze.

Sophie Maddaloni appointed General Secretary of Kering

On September 1, 2026, Sophie Maddaloni was appointed General Secretary of Kering, effective immediately, joining the Group Executive Committee and reporting to Jean-Marc Duplaix, in his capacity as Group Chief Operating Officer. In her new role, she is responsible for the Group's governance and for

safeguarding its interests, as well as for upholding the highest standards of compliance. She oversees the Legal, Internal Control, Internal Audit, and Security departments, working closely with Executive Management and the Board of Directors.

Departure of Anthony Vaccarello from Saint Laurent

On October 9, 2026, Saint Laurent announced the departure of its creative director, Anthony Vaccarello. Over the past decade, Anthony Vaccarello has played a key role in Saint Laurent's development, helping to strengthen its identity and influence across the worlds of fashion and culture. The House will soon announce its new creative leadership.

Departure of Seán McGirr from Alexander McQueen

On October 16, 2026, Alexander McQueen announced the departure of its creative director, Seán McGirr. Since joining Alexander McQueen in 2023, Seán has shaped a new chapter in the House’s creative story, bringing a distinctive vision while staying deeply connected to the spirit and legacy of its founder, Lee

Alexander McQueen. The House will soon announce its new creative leadership.

About Kering

Kering is a global, family-led luxury group, home to people whose passion and expertise nurture creative Houses across couture and ready-to-wear, leather goods, jewelry, eyewear and beauty: Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga, Alexander McQueen, Brioni, Boucheron, Pomellato, DoDo, Qeelin, Ginori 1735, as well as Kering Eyewear. Inspired by their creative heritage, Kering Houses design and craft exceptional products and experiences that reflect the Group’s commitment to excellence, sustainability and culture. This vision is expressed in our signature: Creativity is our Legacy. In 2025, Kering employed 44,000 people and generated

revenue of €14.7 billion.
